issues.body: `gen_graphs` returns `Ok(None)` as soon as any graph term map produces NULL, and `emit_row` then skips the whole row or predicate-object map. R2RML graph sets are unions of the graphs generated by their graph maps: a NULL term map generates no graph, but it must not erase graphs generated by sibling maps or by the other side of the subject/POM union. For example, with subject `rr:graph rr:defaultGraph` and a POM graph template whose column is empty, the POM statement must still be emitted in the default graph. The new `r2rml_default_graph_constant_joins_the_union` test instead expects that statement to be absent for row 2, making the test assert the incorrect behavior.
issues.fix_hint: Make graph generation collect every non-NULL graph independently; NULL should contribute nothing rather than return an outer `None`. Then union the surviving subject and POM graph sets. Preserve the distinction between (a) no graph maps declared, which means the default graph, and (b) graph maps declared but all producing NULL, which generates no statements for that scope. Add or correct tests covering a NULL POM graph map alongside a valid subject graph, a NULL subject graph map alongside a valid POM graph, and multiple graph maps where only one is NULL.
issues.title: NULL graph maps incorrectly suppress statements from other graphs

verdict.summary: The named-graph implementation has a major R2RML correctness error: a NULL-producing graph map is treated as annihilating the entire graph set rather than contributing no graph to the union. This can silently drop statements that should still be emitted into another valid subject- or predicate-object-map graph. The newly added default-graph test explicitly codifies the wrong result, so the test does not protect the specified invariant.
